key_insight: Per-matrix SVD is locally optimal, but better low-rank compression comes from optimizing across matrices, Transformer blocks, and the full language model in sequence.
engineering_relevance: For LLM compression, treating each matrix independently can leave accuracy on the table; a three-level refinement chain yields much better perplexity at the same compression rate.
method: L1: whitened SVD truncation for each matrix
L2: block-level joint optimization across compressed matrices
L3: end-to-end language-model loss refinement using 256 calibration sequences
evidence_signal: On LLaMA-7B at 60% compression, WikiText-2 perplexity improved from 42.1 to 19.1 to 11.4 across the three stages, with gains reported across 20-80% compression and multiple architectures.
watch_item: The reported cross-architecture and compression-sweep results use architecture-specific setups, and the method improves perplexity/compression fidelity rather than downstream task accuracy.
paper_title: Per-Matrix Optimality Is Not Enough: Three-Level Optimization for Low-Rank LLM Compression
